title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page continues the previous one, which ends by forming a category of fractions in which universal homeomorphisms are made invertible. Grothendieck draws a general consequence: an 'anabelian' statement for étale topoi, phrased relative to a base S.

(1) Setting. S is a locally noetherian base scheme; the margin queries 'S de car. 0 ?'. Consider the category of reduced S-schemes locally of finite presentation. Consider the functor X ↦ X_et into the 2-category of topoi over S_et; the transcription reads 'Set', but the context, morphisms 'au-dessus de S_et', makes S_et the likely reading.

(2) First claim: the functor is 1-faithful. If f, g : X ⇉ Y are S-morphisms whose induced topos morphisms f_et, g_et : X_et ⇉ Y_et over S_et are isomorphic (2-isomorphic), then f = g.

(3) Second claim: the functor becomes fully faithful after passing to the category of fractions of (Sch_{l.t.f}/S) obtained by inverting universal homeomorphisms. Inverting them is forced, because universal homeomorphisms induce equivalences of étale topoi (topological invariance of the étale site, SGA 1 IX 4.10 / SGA 4 VIII). This is essentially Grothendieck's conjecture that, over suitably arithmetic bases, the étale topos determines a scheme and its maps up to universal homeomorphism.

(4) Illustration: X is a proper algebraic curve over a field k of finite type over Q, and K = k(X) is its function field. Unwinding the statement should recover the 'fact' that every outer automorphism of E_K which respects the structure (the map to Gal_k = Γ_k) and commutes with the Γ-action comes from an automorphism of X. This is the birational / Galois-theoretic anabelian statement for curves over finitely generated fields.

The page serves the 'Longue Marche' programme: anabelian reconstruction of arithmetic schemes from Galois groups and étale topoi. It leads into §3 on the next page, the study of sections of E_U → E_K, i.e. the section conjecture.
errors: As stated, for an arbitrary locally noetherian S, full faithfulness is false. Over S = Spec C, or any algebraically closed field, S_et = Set, and étale topoi of varieties see only (profinite) topology: non-isomorphic curves of the same genus have equivalent étale topoi. Some arithmetic hypothesis on S (finite type over Q, or similar) is needed, as the surrounding pages implicitly assume.

In characteristic p even 1-faithfulness fails before localization. Over S = Spec F_p, the absolute Frobenius of X is an S-morphism different from the identity, yet it induces a topos morphism isomorphic to the identity. The margin query 'S de car. 0 ?' correctly flags this. Even after inverting universal homeomorphisms, Frobenius becomes a nontrivial automorphism inducing the trivial topos map, so positive characteristic requires extra care.
Reducedness is needed, since nilpotent thickenings are invisible to the étale topos. Grothendieck indeed inserted 'réduits' as a correction.

The final application ('on retrouverait le "fait"') is heuristic. Passing from the étale-topos statement for X to a statement about the Galois group of the function field K requires a limit/birational argument that is not given. Grothendieck himself puts 'fait' in quotes.

ideas.what: X ↦ X_et is 1-faithful on reduced schemes of finite presentation over S, and fully faithful after inverting universal homeomorphisms (anabelian conjecture for étale topoi).
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck's conjecture on reconstruction of schemes from étale topoi (étale-topos anabelian conjecture)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck, letter to Faltings (1983) as conjecture; Voevodsky (c. 1990) proved the isomorphism version for normal schemes of finite type over finitely generated fields of char 0; Carlson–Haine–Wolf (2024) for more general schemes up to universal homeomorphism
ideas.where_published: Letter to G. Faltings (1983), printed in Geometric Galois Actions I (1997); Esquisse d'un programme alludes to the anabelian programme

ideas.what: Universal homeomorphisms induce equivalences of étale topoi, hence must be inverted for full faithfulness.
ideas.modern_name: Topological invariance of the étale site

ideas.what: Outer automorphisms of the Galois group of the function field of a curve over a finitely generated field of char 0 that are compatible with the projection to Γ_k come from automorphisms of the curve.
ideas.modern_name: Birational anabelian conjecture for curves (Galois characterisation of function fields)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (conjecture); Pop (1990s), Mochizuki and others for proofs; Neukirch–Uchida for number fields
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings (1983); Esquisse d'un programme (1984)

missed.claim: The page splits the étale-topos anabelian conjecture into two parts, stated relative to a general locally noetherian base S. The first is 1-faithfulness (2-isomorphic induced topos maps imply equal morphisms) before any localization. The second is full faithfulness only after inverting universal homeomorphisms. It also explicitly flags characteristic 0 as a likely hypothesis. This is an early, slightly more relative and refined formulation than the version usually quoted from the Faltings letter, but the content is essentially known and credited to Grothendieck.
missed.quote: le foncteur X ↦ X_et ... est 1-fidèle ... et devient pleinement fidèle, quand on passe à la catégorie des fractions ... en rendant inversibles les homéom. universels
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Recent work (Carlson–Haine–Wolf) on reconstruction from étale topoi treats Isom and Hom versions; the separate 1-faithfulness statement over a general base, with the char-0 caveat, is a clean formulation that could be cited as Grothendieck's original framing. Historically minor.

deep.surprise_reason: The page states, in draft form, the étale-topos version of the anabelian conjecture that Grothendieck published in his 1983 letter to Faltings, proved in parts by Voevodsky and Carlson–Haine–Wolf. The relative 1-faithful / fully-faithful split and the char-0 margin note are nice details but not new mathematics.
transcription_corrections: '2-catégorie des topos au-dessus de Set' and 'au-dessus de Set' should most likely read 'S_et' (étale topos of the base S), not 'Set'.
Margin note reads 'S de car. 0 ?', a query on the characteristic hypothesis, justified by the Frobenius counterexample in char p.
'f_et, g_et' is an interlinear insertion under 'f,g : X ⇉ Y' labelling the induced topos morphisms.
'Exprimant par ceci' could be 'Explicitant ceci'; uncertain.
'Gal_k' in 'respecte la structure : Gal_k' is probably the projection E_K → Γ_k (Galois group of the base field k); reading uncertain.
